questions.question: What is monolithic architecture?

options.text: A single deployable unit containing all application functionality

questions.explanation: Monolithic: entire application as one unit. All features in single codebase, single deployment, single process. Traditional approach. Examples: early eBay, early Amazon, many enterprise apps.

questions.question: What is a key advantage of monolithic architecture?

options.text: Simpler development, testing, and deployment—especially for smaller teams

questions.explanation: Monolith advantages: simple deployment (one artifact), easy debugging (single process), no network latency between components, simpler transactions, lower operational complexity. Great for startups and MVPs.

questions.question: What is the 'big ball of mud' problem in monoliths?

options.text: Code becomes tangled and interdependent over time, making changes risky and difficult

questions.explanation: Big ball of mud: no clear boundaries, everything depends on everything. Change one thing, break another. Symptoms: fear of refactoring, long regression testing, 'don't touch that code'. Technical debt accumulation.

questions.question: How does a monolith typically scale?

options.text: Vertical scaling (bigger server) or horizontal scaling (multiple identical instances)

questions.explanation: Monolith scaling: vertical (more CPU/RAM) or horizontal (clone entire app behind load balancer). Problem: can't scale components independently. CPU-heavy feature? Scale everything. Wasteful but simple.

questions.question: What is the deployment challenge with monolithic applications?

options.text: Any change requires redeploying the entire application, increasing risk and downtime

questions.explanation: Deployment risk: small bug fix = redeploy everything. Long build times, extensive testing needed. Coordination required across teams. Deployment windows become bottlenecks. Rollback = rollback everything.

questions.question: What is a modular monolith?

options.text: A monolith with well-defined internal module boundaries that could later become services

questions.explanation: Modular monolith: best of both worlds. Clear module boundaries, defined interfaces, but single deployment. Easier to maintain than spaghetti monolith. Can evolve to microservices if needed. Shopify uses this.

questions.question: When is monolithic architecture the right choice?

options.text: For startups, MVPs, small teams, and when domain boundaries are unclear

questions.explanation: Monolith fits: early-stage products (speed to market), small teams (less coordination), unclear domains (easier to refactor), simple applications. Start monolith, extract services when pain points emerge.

questions.question: What is the technology stack limitation of monoliths?

options.text: Typically locked to one language/framework for the entire application

questions.explanation: Tech stack lock-in: entire app in one language. Can't use Python for ML, Go for performance-critical parts. Upgrading framework affects everything. Microservices allow polyglot—right tool for each job.

questions.question: How does team scaling work with monolithic architecture?

options.text: Becomes difficult as teams grow—merge conflicts, coordination overhead, unclear ownership

questions.explanation: Team scaling challenges: shared codebase = merge conflicts, stepping on toes. Unclear ownership. Long CI/CD queues. Conway's Law: org structure mirrors architecture. Large teams → pressure to split.

questions.question: What is the 'monolith first' approach?

options.text: Start with a monolith, then extract microservices as you understand the domain better

questions.explanation: Monolith first (Martin Fowler): premature microservices = wrong boundaries. Start monolith, learn domain, identify seams, extract services. Easier to split monolith than merge bad microservices.

questions.question: What happens when a monolith crashes?
questions.explanation: Single point of failure: one bug can crash entire app. Memory leak in one feature = everything down. Mitigation: multiple instances, health checks, auto-restart. But bug affects all instances equally.

questions.question: Your startup has 5 developers building an MVP. Should you use monolithic or microservices architecture?

options.text: Monolith—simpler, faster development, appropriate for team size and stage

questions.explanation: Startup MVP: monolith wins. Speed to market critical. Small team can't handle microservices operational complexity. Domain not yet understood. Build monolith, validate product, refactor later if successful.
